metadata.source: Michael Hahn: "Kṣemendras Garbhāvakrāntyavadāna (Sanskrittexte aus dem tibetischen Tanjur II)", Journal of the European Ayurvedic Society 5 (1997), pp. 82-112. = KAvk_10

children.translated_text: Dwelling on the bank of the spotless lotus pond at the edge of the camp (<s>campā</s>),
the Teacher (<s>Śāstā</s>), formerly engaged in bestowing grace upon all worlds,
when asked by the <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Ānanda</s>, who was desirous of understanding the [process of] touch (?),
described the course of birth of beings from the commencement of conception onward. (KĀvk 10.1)
By white, black, and variegated threads of <s>karma</s> belonging to embodied beings,
the wondrous garment of birth, of manifold conditions, is seen in the world—
even when it is worn out, the attachment clinging to it, soiled by afflictions,

children.text: yasyātyantaṃ cirapariṇater naiva niryāti rāgaḥ // KAvk_10.2 //
children.translated_text: that passion (<s>rāga</s>) of long maturation never fully departs despite all efforts. (KĀvk 10.2)

children.text: puṃsaḥ śukraṃ vigalitadhṛter ārtavaṃ yoṣitaś ca
children.translated_text: The semen (<s>śukra</s>) of a man whose self-control has dissolved, and the menstrual blood (<s>ārtava</s>) of a woman,
in the union of the two, joined in the intermingling of the excitement of touch—

children.text: ekībhūtaṃ vrajati niyamāt kasya cid bījabhāvaṃ
children.translated_text: merged together, it inevitably assumes the nature of a seed,

children.text: yo 'ntas tasmin bhavati sahasā saṃnikāṣe yathāgniḥ // KAvk_10.3 //
children.translated_text: within which something suddenly arises, like fire in contact [with fuel]. (KĀvk 10.3)
An effusion of passion, a crystal fragment, a cloud, ocean water,

children.text: puṣpāmodas tilaṃ iva śanaiḥ kāñcanaṃ vāgnitāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: the fragrance of flowers, a sesame seed, gold [heated by] fire's heat—

children.text: so 'yaṃ garbhaṃ viśati niyatair apy asaṃlakṣyavṛttir
children.translated_text: this [being] enters the womb, its activity imperceptible even to the determined,

children.text: vāyur gandhair iva bahuvidhaiḥ karmabhir vāsyamānaḥ // KAvk_10.4 //
children.translated_text: like wind permeated by manifold scents, imbued with [various] <s>karmas</s>. (KĀvk 10.4)
In that [womb], developing through subtle stages, resembling a fish-residue (?),
though of wondrous form with abundant and varied configurations, it remains imperceptible.

children.text: kaṃ cit kālaṃ vahati vikṛtiṃ nirvikārāyamāno
children.translated_text: For some time it undergoes transformation while appearing unchanging,

children.text: māyūrāṇḍe jalamaya iva vyaktabhaktir mayūraḥ // KAvk_10.5 //
children.translated_text: like a peacock within its egg, watery in form, [yet with] its features latent. (KĀvk 10.5)
There, from implantation (<s>ādhāna</s>), passing through the stages of dense tendril, thorn, fleshy mass, and so forth,
leaving behind each successive [stage], being cooked by the heat generated in the belly,
that [being], through the sequence of turning <s>karmas</s> in nine full months,

children.text: kleśaṃ bhuṅkte kim api viṣamaṃ duḥkhasaṃjñāprapannaḥ // KAvk_10.6 //
children.translated_text: suffers some indescribable extreme anguish, having arrived at the state called 'suffering' (<s>duḥkha</s>). (KĀvk 10.6)

children.text: kāle vṛntāt svayaṃ iva phalaṃ vicyutaṃ karmapākāt
children.translated_text: In due time, like a fruit fallen by itself from a stalk through the ripening of <s>karma</s>,
propelled by foul winds of unimpeded swiftness arising at that moment,
laden with bonds of <s>karma</s> that are companions to the abode of repeated practice toward a mark,

children.text: niryāty antaḥ śara iva dhanuryantraṇair yantramuktaḥ // KAvk_10.7 //
children.translated_text: it emerges from within like an arrow released from the mechanism of a bow's tension. (KĀvk 10.7)

body.text:
uttānāsyaḥ saralarasanaś cūcukāgraṃ lihānaḥ
stanyaṃ mātuḥ pibati yad asau naiva karṇena nākṣṇā / janmābhyāsavyasanayatanāyāsasaṃvāsalinā

children.translated_text: that instructs it in all skills even before [conscious awareness]. (KĀvk 10.8)

body.translated_text: Lying face up with straightened tongue, licking the tip of the nipple, it drinks the mother's breast-milk—not by ear, not by eye; it is the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) alone, clinging through the affliction of habitual practice from [past] births,

children.translated_text: Pervaded within by stitched [channels] with their various divisions for experiencing diverse sense-objects,
like a lotus fiber with its clearly spread threads, permeated by filaments (?),
that bewildered one, given awareness by the senses—companions of [its] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>)—
recognizes the nurse through the breast-milk, speech, form, fragrance, and touch. (KĀvk 10.9)
Tormented by the pulling of hands, by the rubbing of bedclothes,
with trembling body at every spot, being eaten by insects,
constantly crying, bereft of speech, [enduring] the affliction of bodily suffering—

children.text: kaṃ bobrūte viṣamavipadām āspadatvaṃ prayātaḥ // KAvk_10.10 //
children.translated_text: to whom does it cry out, having become the abode of terrible misfortunes? (KĀvk 10.10)
With face smeared by streams of milk spurting forth, regurgitated under pressure,
sprinkled by [the milk] that has fallen upon its upturned chest, it is seen—
in the bold sport of <s>Māyā's</s> play that steals away memory,
as if [enveloped] by laughter, its body thoroughly pervaded by radiant [milk]. (KĀvk 10.11)
Then, when the time of learning to write arrives, with hand set down carelessly,
in this <s>saṃsāra</s>, in the activities of drawing bound letters with unwavering [hand],

children.text: janmāvartaṃ nijaṃ iva likhan dīrghaṃ oṃkāram ādau
children.translated_text: as though inscribing the long cycle of its own births, [writing] the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> at first,

children.text: varge varge vitarati matiṃ bhogasarge niviṣṭaḥ // KAvk_10.12 //
children.translated_text: it applies its mind to group after group [of letters], engaged in the creation of [worldly] enjoyments. (KĀvk 10.12)
Having attained understanding, somehow emerging from the delusion of childhood,

children.text: kāmautsukyāt punar api pare yauvane naṣṭasaṃjñaḥ /
children.translated_text: yet again in the next [stage of] youth, losing consciousness from the eagerness of desire (<s>kāma</s>),
in the worthless [charms of women that are like] the lightning-flashes of clouds playing in misfortune,

children.text: badhnāty āsthāṃ sthirataradhiyā yoṣitāṃ vibhrameṣu // KAvk_10.13 //
children.translated_text: with ever-firmer resolve it binds its faith to the allurements of women. (KĀvk 10.13)

children.text: vāci śrotraṃ vapur api calāliṅganeṣv aṅganānāṃ
children.translated_text: [Placing] the ear on their speech, the body too in the fleeting embraces of women,
the nose on the fragrance of their face-breath, the taste on that [breath's] flavor,

children.text: pātre kurvan dṛśam api mukhe suptasarvakriyo 'sau
children.translated_text: placing the eye too upon their faces as a vessel—all its faculties asleep—
it holds all its senses as though they were measures fitted to the body [of women]. (KĀvk 10.14)
That lustful one, habitually given to hating what is near, despises the beloved,
ever seeking fresh new pleasures, he desires another, striving ardently for another's love—
Thus, a witness to the embarrassment unseen in [their] mutually unfitting conduct,
his desire (<s>kāma</s>), naturally tasteless, with its variegated workings, serves only for laughter. // KAvk 10.15 //
Drowning and clinging in the ocean of sense-objects with its shallow foundation,
fallen, his path obstructed — like an elephant in mud —
a swoon of delusion arises, devoid of any understanding of what should be done,
led to blindness by youth that lasts but a few days. // KAvk 10.16 //
For as long as he wanders and moves about, delights and stretches himself,
speaking with smiling, smiling [words], with limbs bent in the embrace of passion,
for just that long, there falls upon him, released by Time,
a garland of death disguised as white old age, [white] as licked frost. // KAvk 10.17 //
Moment by moment, in the passage of time, under the power of the sleep of delusion,

children.text: prāptaṃ nāsmin vapuṣi sukṛtaṃ naiva dattaṃ na bhuktaṃ /
children.translated_text: no merit has been gained in this body, nothing given, nothing enjoyed.

children.text: itthaṃ caurair iva sa muṣitaś cintayaty eva duḥkhāt
children.translated_text: Thus, robbed as if by thieves, he reflects only on suffering —
that heedlessness of despair, whose fruit is remorse, [belongs] to the deluded. // KAvk 10.18 //
When that youth, like a spring of graceful women and flowering vines, has departed —
that dreamlike youth, weighed on the scale of wealth acquired by evil deeds —
his entire nature destroyed, with all his limbs wearied and dispassionate,

children.text: rājyabhraṃśe nṛpa iva sukhaṃ so 'tha śocaty atītaṃ // KAvk_10.19 //
children.translated_text: like a king upon loss of his kingdom, he then grieves for the pleasures that are past. // KAvk 10.19 //

body.text: āyur nītaṃ na ca samucitaṃ yācakāyopanītaṃ

children.text: nāpy unnītaṃ diśi diśi yaśaḥ satpathaṃ na pratītaṃ
children.translated_text: nor has fame been raised in every direction; the virtuous path has not been followed;
the poison of begging has been drunk, and what was gained was abundant in the fever of sorrow;

children.text: bhītaṃ pāpāt kim api na mayā yat tad eva praṇītaṃ // KAvk_10.20 //
children.translated_text: I have not even feared sin — whatever was [done], that alone was [my] accomplishment." // KAvk 10.20 //

body.translated_text: "My life has been spent, yet nothing fitting has been offered to any supplicant;

children.translated_text: "Where is that captivating beauty of youth that stole the splendor of golden trees?
And where is this body, its shade decayed like a tree eaten by worms?
From afar, these young women, averting their eyes, hiding in corners,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ śītaṃ tarum iva vane vānaraṃ māṃ vadanti // KAvk_10.21 //
children.translated_text: call me — like a monkey on a dry, cold tree in the forest." // KAvk 10.21 //

children.text: so 'yaṃ kāyaḥ śrayati vilayaṃ naiva māyānikāyaḥ
children.translated_text: "This very body is heading toward destruction, this aggregate of illusion;

children.text: srastāḥ sarve daśanamaṇayas te ca keśāḥ na doṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: the gems of teeth have all fallen out, and those hairs — they are not faults [but signs of decay];
the wind [of disease] strikes at the vitality of the limbs — not a sprout of delusion [remains];
and even for me, wasted and confined to my bed, this thirst knows no end." // KAvk 10.22 //
Having reflected thus, afflicted by irregular gasps and hiccups spreading forth,
he is ready to suddenly abandon the worldly journey he has followed for so long.
Become mute, his composure shattered, he contemplates separation from his kin,

children.text: śakticchedād ṛṇaṃ iva mahat prāptakālo daridraḥ // KAvk_10.23 //
children.translated_text: like a destitute man whose time has come [to repay] a great debt, through loss of his resources. // KAvk 10.23 //

children.text: bhūmiṃ gehaṃ vasu parijanaṃ putradārādi cānyat
children.translated_text: Land, house, wealth, retinue, sons, wife, and other things —
he reckons them all in his mind at the time when life is at its end.

children.text: yāvaj janmany api punar asau snehamohānubandhais
children.translated_text: Even in the next birth, through the bonds of attachment and delusion,

children.text: tais tair antaḥ kṛtaparicayas tanmayībhāvam eti // KAvk_10.24 //
children.translated_text: familiarized inwardly with each of those, he attains a state of absorption in them. // KAvk 10.24 //
Having endured suffering born of unbearable evil <s>karma</s> (deeds) in the midst of thousands of cauldrons,
he revolves through wombs in the hells of <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, and others.

children.text: yad vā puṇyakalārjitaṃ sukhapadaṃ tat saṃkṣaye duḥkhadaṃ
children.translated_text: Or whatever happiness was earned by a fraction of merit — that, when exhausted, gives suffering.
Therefore, let one of purified intellect concentrate [the mind] for the attainment of the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>). // KAvk 10.25 //
Thus, having taken a vow for the crossing of the terrifying ocean of existence,
the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) instructed [beings] for the attainment of wholesome [states] by sentient beings. // KAvk 10.26 //

body.text: / iti kṣemendraviracitāyāṃ bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatāyāṃ garbhāvakrāntinirdeśo nāma daśamaḥ pallavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter (<s>pallava</s>), named "The Instruction on Entry into the Womb" (<s>Garbhāvakrāntinirdeśa</s>), in the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā</s> composed by <s>Kṣemendra</s>.
